objective: maximize cumulative user profit while enforcing verified-publication hard minimums and minimizing user intervention

hardPublicationPolicy.rule: Expected-profit optimization may choose WHICH qualified products to publish, but may not reduce the verified-publication floor or erase carried debt.

pcAvailabilityPolicy.assumption: User normally closes Windows PC after 01:00 JST.
pcAvailabilityPolicy.after0100: Do not require Windows publisher execution. Continue cloud research, build preparation, queue/state/ledger repair and fallback preparation.
pcAvailabilityPolicy.frontLoadRule: Debt and current-day publication minimums must be pushed toward verified public state before 01:00; do not depend on post-01:00 local execution.

runPlan.goal: Service oldest debt first; if either active item remains blocked after brief diagnosis, defer and switch immediately.
Add verified publications with already-proven adjacent assets and strong purchase intent.
Publish distinct qualified fallback products; preserve quality and strict commerce verification.
Continue quota recovery; do not let one failed item consume the cycle.
Close remaining daily minimums where possible; prepare late-day catch-up queue.
Use additional distinct candidates if quota/debt remains; otherwise advance Microsoft Store submission-ready work.
Late catch-up: prioritize any remaining debt/target shortfall while Windows is still expected available.
Final PC-dependent recovery window before 01:00; verify formally or carry exact residual debt forward without clearing it.

productionRunPolicy.normalCompletion: At least one newly verified public artifact per PC-available production run when debt or quota remains, with multiple publications encouraged when safe qualified candidates are ready.
productionRunPolicy.blockedCandidate: Diagnose briefly; if strict publication cannot be reached, defer and switch to another qualified candidate rather than ending the run.
nonCompletionEvidence: HTTP/title-only evidence when commerce checks are required

note: note official analysis of about 300k paid articles reports paid-article sales +26.8% YoY and creator count +42.0% YoY; AI utilization +268.6%, SNS/content operations +258.7%, side jobs/remote work +179.0%.

note recommendation-engine testing reported category impressions 4.3x YoY, PV 2.2x and internal circulation 1.5x in January 2026, supporting high-specificity topical content rather than generic duplication.

PTA operational guidance updated June 2026 explicitly identifies role allocation and standardized handover as recurring organizational problems, supporting adjacent small-organization workflow products.
MicrosoftStore: Microsoft states the Store serves over 250 million monthly active users and allows non-game apps to use their own commerce and retain 100% of revenue.

Current Store search surfaced many direct image-resizer/compressor and file-renamer competitors, while the CSV search surfaced fewer direct Japanese CSV-cleanup-style results; therefore CSV cleanup/deduplication is ranked above generic image resizing and generic rename utilities for the next experiment.

profitRules: Debt and today's verified-publication floor are first priority.
Within that floor, prefer stronger purchase intent, differentiation, conversion fit and expected net profit.
Use existing public assets to create coherent bundles before inventing unrelated BOOTH products.
Do not publish plaintext paid assets to GitHub.
Do not infer public URLs; independently verify them before marking completed or linking funnels.
Use actual sales/message evidence when available; do not invent demand metrics.
Avoid low-value near duplicates; switch to a distinct qualified fallback when needed.
Do not reactivate KDP or LINE without explicit user instruction.

MicrosoftStore.status: initial app publication route proven; next research priority is a local-first CSV cleanup/deduplication utility; no repository performance metrics available yet
